issues.title: amdgpu: recurring gfxhub page fault (PERMISSION_FAULTS=0x3) on Navi 22 / RX 6700 XT — gfx ring wedge, use-after-free pattern, 3 apps (kwin, Chrome, Rocket League/DXVK)
issues.author: Thomas Ratouit (Thoratou)
issues.description:
## Environment

| Item | Incident 1 (2026-08-31) | Incident 4 (2026-09-03) | Incident 8 (2026-09-05) |
|------|--------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------|
| Kernel | `6.18.42-1-cachyos-lts` | `7.2.2-1-cachyos` | `7.2.2-1-cachyos` |
| Mesa | `26.2.1` | `26.2.2` | `26.2.2` |
| GPU | AMD Navi 22 `1002:73df` rev c1, Radeon RX 6700 XT, 12272 MiB VRAM (ASUS `1043:05c9`) | same | same |
| Compositor | KDE Plasma 6 / KWin Wayland | same | same |
| amdgpu params | stock, no overclock, no `pp_od_clk_voltage` | same | same |

Cmdline: `quiet splash rw rootflags=subvol=/@ root=UUID=... usbcore.autosuspend=-1 pcie_aspm=off`

## Summary

**Three** GPU faults across three independent application vectors with the same amdgpu
signature on the same board. The blamed VMID process changes each time (kwin, Chrome, Rocket
League) — consistent with a buffer-lifetime race in whichever client was submitting at the
moment, not a per-process bug.

Common signature: `[gfxhub] page fault` (`src_id:0 ring:24`), UTCL2 client `0x1b`,
**`PERMISSION_FAULTS: 0x3`**, `WALKER_ERROR: 0x0`, `MAPPING_ERROR: 0x0`. The GPU touched
pages absent from the process page tables while executing an IB → buffer freed / PTEs torn
down while still referenced by the submission. Not thermal (60 °C junction, 110 °C crit),
not a walker/mapping error.

- Incident 1: `gfx_0.1.0` wedged in a reset loop (~8 resets), ring seq barely advanced
  (1265044 → 1265054), system froze, hard reset required.

issues.author: Hlib Kanunnikov
issues.description:
# [Regression][SMU13][Navi 33] Runtime resume restores stale 30 W limit against `[100,120]`, wedging RX 7700S

## Brief summary of the problem:

Runtime resume of the discrete Navi 33 GPU can restore a power limit cached
under the previous power-source conditions. After a battery-to-AC transition,
AMDGPU attempts to restore `30 W` while the firmware reports a valid range of
`[100,120]`. The write is rejected and a later runtime resume can fail in the
SMU block with `-22`, leaving the dGPU in `power/runtime_status=error` until
reboot.

The same machine previously reproduced the opposite `100 W` against `[30,30]`
failure on Linux 6.18.40. Linux 6.18.42 included the stable fix for the current
power-limit getter and stopped that direction from reproducing in a controlled
test, but the reverse `30 W` against `[100,120]` case remained. It now reproduces
again on Linux 6.18.44 with August 2026 AMD firmware.

The broken dGPU later causes suspend and hibernation failures, including
`amdgpu_pmops_freeze` returning `-121`, but those are downstream effects: the
journal proves the dGPU runtime-resume failure occurred hours before the first
hibernation request.

issues.author: Jason Eggleston
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

After every suspend-to-RAM (S3), small blocks of pixels in long-lived textures come back with a wrong uniform color. Here it shows in the KDE Plasma wallpaper as a few 2-3 px blocks of saturated magenta/blue on a dark background.

The damage is permanent — redrawing does not clear it, and it survives further suspends — until that texture is re-uploaded. It reproduces on every S3 cycle, and it accumulates: each suspend adds new bad blocks while the old ones stay at identical coordinates. A wallpaper is one of the few surfaces uploaded once and never rewritten, which is why it is visible there and easy to miss elsewhere.

Expected: a buffer evicted to system RAM and restored comes back byte-identical. Actual: some blocks differ, including a wrong alpha channel on a fully opaque surface.

Cause: on resume the kernel does not restore DCC surfaces, it re-encodes them from scratch, and the re-encode is not bit-exact. In `amdgpu_ttm_copy_mem_to_mem()`, a GTT -\> VRAM move of a DCC BO sets `AMDGPU_COPY_FLAGS_WRITE_COMPRESSED` and recompresses using parameters read back from the BO's tiling flags. I verified those parameters are correct and stable for the affected surface, so this is not userspace supplying bad metadata.

Note this is not suspend-specific: `amdgpu_bo_move()` is TTM's move callback, so any eviction of a DCC BO takes the same round trip. Suspend is just a reliable trigger because it forces every buffer through at once.

I guess the IOMMU tells the memory controller to transparantly decrypts the memory for the GPU anyway so it is supported and the new rejection in `drivers/iommu/dma-iommu.c` is wrong?

issues.author: Igor Marques
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

Twice in 48 hours (2026-08-25 16:14 and 2026-08-26 15:50), the GPU stopped delivering interrupts entirely. The amdgpu MSI counter in `/proc/interrupts` froze to the exact same value across repeated samples while the GPU kept executing work: fence sequence numbers kept advancing, signaled only by the 500ms fence fallback timers. Both displays froze on their last frame (flip_done timed out on both CRTCs), ttm kworkers piled up in D state, load climbed to ~16, and the desktop was unusable while SSH stayed fully functional.

During the second incident I inspected the IH block live with umr and found `IH_RB_WPTR.RB_OVERFLOW=1` with the WPTR still advancing, the RPTR frozen, and `WPTR_OVERFLOW_CLEAR` never set: the ring had overflowed and the driver's overflow handling never ran (dmesg has no "IH ring buffer overflow" line on either day). With `IH_RB_CNTL.RPTR_REARM=1` that state is terminal: the IH waits for a rptr update that never comes and never raises another MSI. Clearing the overflow flag and realigning the RPTR by hand, with the machine still in the failed state, brought interrupt delivery back within seconds. That experiment is the core evidence of this report.

Frequency: two occurrences in 48 hours so far, at seemingly random moments of ordinary desktop use, with no reliable reproducer yet. My journal history (back to Aug 07) contains no earlier occurrence of this signature.

issues.title: NULL deref in dal_ddc_open (pin_clock->pin) on DP HPD after sink power-down; kworker dies with IRQs off and the machine hard-wedges
issues.author: Dennis T.
issues.description:
## Brief summary

DPMS-off of all outputs, then the monitors drop their DP links. amdgpu handles the HPD as a full `link_detect` / `retrieve_link_cap` and oopses in `dal_ddc_open()`:

```
RIP: dal_ddc_open+0x8c/0x150 [amdgpu]
BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000028
Workqueue: events_highpri dm_irq_work_func [amdgpu]
note: kworker/1:0H[29] exited with irqs disabled
```

`dal_gpio_open_ex(ddc->pin_clock)` returned `GPIO_RESULT_OK`, but `ddc->pin_clock->pin` is NULL. The next instruction reads `pin->store.en` at offset `0x28` with no NULL check. The kworker is killed with IRQs disabled while holding DC AUX/link locks, so the box wedges instead of recovering.

The unguarded deref is still in linux.git `master` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/gpio/gpio_service.c`).

Call chain:

```
handle_hpd_irq_helper
  → link_detect → detect_link_and_local_sink
  → retrieve_link_cap → dpcd_set_source_specific_data
  → dm_dp_aux_transfer → dce_aux_transfer_raw → acquire
  → dal_ddc_open   ← RIP
```

## Suggested fix

`dal_ddc_open()` already bails if `dal_gpio_open_ex()` returns an error. It does **not** check that the resulting `gpio->pin` is non-NULL before `FROM_HW_GPIO_PIN()`. `dal_gpio_service_open()` would have returned an error if `get_ddc_pin()` was NULL at open time, so a successful open with a NULL pin a few instructions later is a lifetime race (concurrent close vs HPD AUX). The missing guard turns that race into an oops.

**Issue Description** The DKMS `configure` script produces false positives for `drm_mode_create_hdmi_colorspace_property` and `drm_mode_create_dp_colorspace_property` on older kernels (e.g., v5.17) that only support the 1-argument version of these functions.

**Time-oriented Execution Flow & Root Cause** The issue stems from a missing sandbox isolation wrapper, which causes a sequential state contamination when combined with the Kbuild toolchain.

1. **State Contamination**: A prior synchronous test in the configuration sequence succeeds, leaving a valid `conftest.o` in the top-level build directory.

5. **False Positive**: `objtool` runs, validates the _stale_ `conftest.o` left by step 1, and returns `0`. `AC_KERNEL_COMPILE_IFELSE` catches this `0` and incorrectly defines `HAVE_DRM_MODE_C

The behaviour of writing `r` into the `pp_od_clk_voltage` overdrive interface differs across hardware versions. On some of them, the reset is instant, on others it simply edits the table settings that need to be separately committed with a `c` command.

For example, it resets right away on [SMU 14.0.2](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.2/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/swsmu/smu14/smu_v14_0_2_ppt.c#L2737-L2768) and [SMU 13.0.6](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.2/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/swsmu/smu13/smu_v13_0_6_ppt.c#L2279).

While on [SMU 14.0.0](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.2/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/swsmu/smu14/smu_v14_0.c#L1839-L1846) and [SMU 13.0.5](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.2/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/swsmu/smu13/smu_v13_0_5_ppt.c#L556-L564), the values are staged and need to be committed separately.

This inconsistency appears to go quite far back in hardware, as the values are [committed on Vega20](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.2/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/powerplay/hwmgr/vega20_hwmgr.c#L3119-L3130) but [staged on Navi10](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.2/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/pm/swsmu/smu11/navi10_ppt.c#L2467-L2473).


## How to reproduce the issue:

Set any non-default settings, try to reset, observe if the reset happens right away or needs a commit.

issues.title: amdgpu/amdkfd: BO leak on ENOMEM process teardown poisons the TTM eviction LRU; a later client can deadlock in amdgpu_vm_bo_move()
issues.author: BocajGnuoy
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

When a GPU client that holds a KFD compute VM dies on an allocation failure
while GTT is exhausted, its buffer objects are left stranded on
`process_info`'s lists at VM teardown. `amdgpu_amdkfd_gpuvm_destroy_cb()` trips
two `WARN_ON`s and frees `process_info` anyway. The orphaned BO stays in TTM's
eviction LRU with `bo_va`s pointing into the freed `amdgpu_vm`, so the **next**
process to trigger eviction spins forever in `amdgpu_vm_bo_move()` ->
`_raw_spin_lock()`. That produces repeating RCU stalls, blocks reclaim-related
work, and eventually makes the machine unusable — within about ten minutes here,
requiring a hard power cycle.

Expected: an allocation failure is reported to userspace, the client exits, and
the driver reclaims its memory. Observed: a recoverable `ENOMEM` leaves the
driver in a state where a subsequent `GEM_CREATE` that forces TTM eviction can
deadlock.

Reproducible on demand. The survivable half (abort -> teardown WARNs) reproduces
on every attempt and needs no power cycle. The full deadlock has been reproduced
and does require one.

Note the abort itself is survivable — it is the relaunch that kills the machine.
Anything that automatically restarts a failed GPU workload can therefore trigger
the second stage without user intervention, which is how I first hit it.

issues.title: deadlock on hibernation in ttm_device_prepare_hibernation() -> throttle_direct_reclaim()
issues.author: Maciej S. Szmigiero
issues.description:
From time to time I get a deadlock when hibernating a machine with amdgpu in `amdgpu_device_prepare()` -> `amdgpu_device_evict_resources()` -> `ttm_device_prepare_hibernation()` -> `ttm_tt_swapout()` -> `shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp()` -> `shmem_get_folio_gfp()` -> `shmem_alloc_and_add_folio()` -> `try_to_free_pages(`) -> `throttle_direct_reclaim()`.

And `throttle_direct_reclaim()` just waits forever for `kswapd` to make progress, which never happens so the machine is essentially deadlocked. 

Looking at the hibernation code it seems that the `prepare` callbacks 
happens *after* tasks are already frozen so no wonder `kswapd` will never make progress.

----

This was reproduced on the latest upstream kernel 7.1.3 but the current drm code does _not_ seem to have any material differences there.

Note this does NOT seem to be duplicate of #5470 since this does _not_ look like memory corruption, just deadlock with page reclaim code.

Also, this does not seem specific to particular type of a amdgpu GPU.

## Summary

issues.title: Display pipeline stall on memory clock speed change with FAMS2 on gfx1201
issues.author: fililip
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

With high enough display bandwidth requirements to trigger SubVP or DRR SubVP reclocking, memory clock P-state changes (automatic or manual DPM) cause the desktop to stall for a few frames, causing a very visible short freeze, which is unlikely to be desired during reclocking.

This turns out to be a faulty hardware lock introduced in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/agd5f/linux/-/commit/00c391102abc13763e2bfc90e05503109b19f074, later renamed in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/agd5f/linux/-/commit/6d92c4d03063480a60bbc3ff61d22197c931f411.

Working around this lock by either removing it entirely or gating it behind a `dmub_hw_lock_mgr_does_context_require_lock` check works flawlessly and eliminates the stall completely: [fams2-mclk-stutter-workaround-minimal.patch](/uploads/09e73a73cacf4c580c8835aceaa574ee/fams2-mclk-stutter-workaround-minimal.patch). I tested this workaround on various different configurations (HDR, VRR, MPO, suspend/resume, hotplugs, etc.) and it never caused any issues. Perhaps it's not needed for dGPUs at all? Especially since without it, SubVP looks like it's doing the correct thing - hiding the clock switch perfectly without any hitches.

Other people report temporary screen blanking rather than stutter on a clock speed change, but it turns out that's due to DRR on some Samsung panels, which seem to blank on VRR on/off transitions. This can be worked around by always setting the `VRR_ENABLED` property to `1` on affected CRT

## Brief summary of the problem:

On an RX 9070 XT (Navi 48 / GFX1201 / DCN 4.0.1), my Samsung Odyssey G70NC connected via DisplayPort randomly loses signal for \~1 second every few minutes when running at high refresh rates with a second monitor connected. Audio output through the monitor also cuts during these drops, confirming a full DisplayPort connection reset rather than just a visual glitch. The secondary Acer K273E connected via HDMI on the same GPU is never affected it remains stable regardless of refresh rate combinations.

The issue is consistently reproducible:

* **Always occurs** with Samsung at 144Hz + Acer at 100Hz
* **Occurs** at various combinations of high refresh rates
* **Completely stable** with both monitors at 60Hz
* **Completely stable** with a single monitor at any refresh rate
